title: VIP Escalation Decision Lifecycle & Weighted Acceptance Playbook
creator: Aria Chen
description: Design a repeatable decision lifecycle and scoring playbook for VIP/top-account feature requests and escalations. The goal is to produce a deterministic intake flow that maps requests to one of four outcomes (Immediate Commit, Timeboxed Sprint, Backlog with SLA, Decline) with an auditable rationale tied to OKRs and capacity. Deliverables: triage matrix, weighting formula, SLA windows, CS/Sales runbook, dashboard wires, and a rollout checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Documented 4-outcome decision matrix with example requests for each bucket
Scoring formula validated against 30 historical top-account requests
Runbook drafted for CS and Sales including SLAs and escalation contact points
Console dashboard prototype showing time-to-decision, commit rate, and cost-risk scores
Stakeholder sign-off from Sales Director and Head of Product
comments: 2025-02-21 — Initial problem framing session with CS (Liam, Priya, Marcus). Agreed on the four outcomes and need for OKR mapping.
2025-02-24 — Collected 32 historical VIP requests from CRM; started labeling signals (revenue, strategic alignment, regulatory risk).
2025-02-27 — Engineering review: noted capacity constraints for Dedicated customers; proposed capacity-adjusted score multiplier.
2025-03-01 — PM review with Sales Director: requested explicit canary/partial-deliverable lanes for >$1M ARR deals.
2025-03-03 — Design critique: recommended simplified UI for intake form with pre-populated account metadata and attachment upload.
decisions: Use weighted scoring with three signal groups: Commercial (ARR, churn risk), Strategic (product fit, referenceability), Operational (data security, regulatory).
Introduce a 'Commit Window' of 10 business days for Immediate Commit candidates; timeboxed sprint window of 30 days for high-confidence partial deliverables.
Capacity multiplier applied to Dedicated-backed requests to reflect reserved throughput costs.
Tie 'Immediate Commit' approvals to OKR owners for final sign-off when ARR > $250k.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot): Runbook and triage matrix applied to 10 live VIP requests (Q2 Week 1)
Phase 2: Dashboard + automated intake form rolled out to CS + Sales (Q2 Week 3)
Phase 3: Integrate scoring into Redwood Console to tag requests and surface to product queues (Q2 Week 6)
Phase 4: Iterate scoring weights based on pilot outcomes and finalize SOP (Q2 Week 8)
next_steps: Finalize scoring weights and run historical simulation (owner: Liam)
Draft CS/Sales runbook and hold training session (owner: Priya)
Mock up dashboard panels and instrument metrics (owner: Omar)
Add intake form fields to Salesforce/Ops and automate webhook to Linear (owner: Tessa)
notes: Avoid creating a fast-track that bypasses technical review; canary lanes should still require an engineering feasibility approval. Consider reserved-capacity cost credits as a negotiation lever with sales for Immediate Commit approvals.
